My top 13:  
  
* **The Red Machine** by a Canadian political writer. This author went to Russia for a few years to complete this English language book about the history of Soviet hockey behind the Iron Curtain. Incredible book. If you liked the Red Army documentary this is a must-read, as it's way, way better than that mediocre documentary.  
* **Road to Olympus** by a notable Soviet hockey architect. Very hard to find and very expensive if you do. Translated in 1968 and way out of print. The architect of the Soviet hockey machine describes his hockey program and gives his thoughts on various other countries' hockey programs - apparently he admired the Swedish players and thought Canadians were barbarians. Who knew?  
* **Open Ice: The Story of a Hockey Legend** by a detailed biographer. Biography of the late defenseman and Hall of Famer who also founded a popular Canadian donut/coffee chain. Goes into tremendous detail as this author always does, and gives a good rundown of the A-, B- and C-forms, which was the system used by teams to acquire players before the entry draft was a thing.  
* **Yzerman: The Making of a Champion** by a detailed biographer. He uses the career of a famous player as a vehicle to analyze the transformation of a well-known hockey organization from perennial loser to unstoppable juggernaut. Even goes into details on the executive careers of notable figures in the sport.  
* **The Rebel League** by a sports historian. Consummate history of a former professional hockey league. Perfectly made book, everything you'd ever want to know.  
* **Net Worth**, by two authors. Similar to the popular book about business adventures, but hockey-themed. A handful of excellent stories related to the business aspect of the NHL.  
* **Power Plays**, by a former league executive. A first-hand account of a former league executive and one-time commissioner of the NHL. Some of this book is obviously biased, as the author had recently been ousted as the commissioner and booted from the Hall of Fame, but there's tons of great info in here.  
* **The Game**, by a legendary goaltender. Nothing needs to be said about this one.  
* **A Life In Hockey**, by a detailed biographer. Not perfect, since this book was finished in 1998 so it's missing later developments, but it does a flawless job of presenting a balanced account of the greatest coach in hockey history.  
* **Ultimate Hockey**, multiple authors. Basically a textbook on the history of the game from the first puck drop to the year 2000. Goes over every major news story that happened and has nice biographies of every star player from each decade.  
* **Thunder and Lightning**, by a former star player // **Playing with Fire**, by another former star player - tie. Great no holds-barred tell-all books by former star players who were never really good at keeping their mouths shut.  
* **Journeyman**, by a former player. He may have only been a role player, but this author is a genuinely great storyteller and this book is enjoyable from start to finish. He had an interesting if not strange career.
